persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
Özkent's Nasdaq bulletin today is devoted to the **Anthropic** IPO: it has been pushed to November, with a target valuation of $2.2 trillion. In his view $34 billion of the headline $42 billion loss is an accounting expense; the real risks are $12.7 billion of 2025 expenses against $4.6 billion of revenue, a $518 billion infrastructure commitment through 2032 (about 80% binding) and a narrow customer base. Of the commitment, $161 billion goes to **Broadcom**, $110 billion to **Amazon**, $111 billion to **Google** and $31.4 billion to **Microsoft**, with the rest most likely going to **Nvidia**.

He is considering a small position of about $35,000 at the IPO and will then watch the trading; he points to **SpaceX**, which fell from $160 to $100 after its IPO and recovered, as an example. His second video is non-financial: it explains a content-creation method for turning hobbies into income, using his wife's example.

items.title: Is Anthropic Worth $2.2 Trillion?
items.summary: Özkent says $34 billion of the $42 billion loss in Anthropic's S-1 is a valuation expense arising from promises made before the IPO, leaving a loss of roughly $8 billion. In 2025 there was $12.7 billion of operating expense against $4.6 billion of revenue, but in 2026 revenue has reached a $100 billion annualized run rate thanks to coding agents. The company plans about $518 billion of spending through 2032; about 80% is binding, with $161 billion going to Broadcom, $110 billion to Amazon, $111 billion to Google and $31.4 billion to Microsoft. It had about $20 billion in cash at the end of 2025, 25% of revenue comes from two customers, and he finds the 80% gross margin figure debatable. In his view US firms pay only $12.5 per user for AI and only 2.2% of individuals pay for it, so the market is very early. The target valuation is $2.2 trillion (about 478 times 2025 revenue, 22 times the $100 billion run rate); the IPO was pushed to November and his view may change once the 2026 figures are published. As a strategy he is considering a small position of about $35,000 at the IPO and then watching the trading.

assets.note: He finds the $2.2 trillion valuation very high; considering a small position of about $35,000 at the IPO.

items.title: How Do You Easily Make Money From Topics You Love?
items.summary: Özkent explains the method from Denko's article through the career-change example of his wife Pınar, for turning hobbies and interests into income. One should first produce content on broad topics and narrow down to sub-topics with a transformation map (the life to avoid, the life to reach, the bridge between them). Objecting to popular ideas creates a front for followers; without expertise, documenting the process of becoming an expert is enough. Pınar has 200,000 followers on LinkedIn and about 91,000 on YouTube; an email newsletter is recommended as your own space, since social media is 'rented land'. Small digital products, coaching and speaking are the income channels; in Turkey special accounts allow collecting social-media income without founding a company. AI is recommended as an aid for idea generation and content planning.

persons.name: Defiant Gatekeeper
persons.digest:
In the first half of the video he drops the Fed chessboard model and looks at the 10-year yield and growth axes: the yield is at its highest since 2006 and growth is high in AI and related sectors, so we are in quadrant "B" and stock performance depends on whether a company's growth beats the bond yield. He reads the Fed's rate hike a few weeks ago not as an independent decision but as theater to prevent market panic. Bond funds lost a lot of money in the first half of the year and lack the cash to lock in yields above 5%, so the short-term direction of yields is hard to call.

In the second half he covers the wild rise in the Pokémon card market: one card sold for about $1 million and another for $8.4 million. He sees both manipulation and genuine demand in the market, thinks this is a dangerous time to enter these old and rare cards, and says the market could see a sharp decline.

items.title: Yield vs growth...and...Pokemon cards...
items.summary: Defiant Gatekeeper first says the chessboard model based on the Fed balance sheet and rates has lost relevance lately because the Fed is doing almost nothing. His new framework is the 10-year yield and growth: quadrant A (low yield, high growth) is the best time and quadrant D (high yield, no growth) the worst. Right now the yield is at its highest since 2006 but growth is high in AI and related sectors, so we are in quadrant B; a stock rises if its growth beats the bond yield and suffers badly if it does not. He interprets the Fed's rate hike a few weeks ago as a staged decision to prevent market panic. According to a hedge-fund bond trader, funds see yields above 5% as an opportunity but lack the liquidity to buy after first-half losses and cash outflows, which may explain why yields are not falling fast. In the second part he describes the extraordinary rise of old, rare and legendary Pokémon cards, with one card selling for about $1 million and a Pikachu card for $8.4 million. He thinks this is not money laundering but could be price inflation between friends, a tax-advantaged inheritance vehicle or a legitimate value transfer. On the real-demand side he gives three wealthy collectors who entered in 2025-2026 (a crypto entrepreneur putting 50% of his wealth in cards, a former investment banker worth $20-30 million, and a founder worth $100-200 million). He concludes that he sees both manipulation and real demand, sets aside at most 5% of his wealth, and thinks the market could fall sharply in the near term.

assets.note: The yield is at its highest since 2006; he says the short-term direction is hard to call and bond funds are seeing cash outflows.

On the power side **CEG** rose 15.8%, **VST** 15.3% and **NRG** 13.4%; he sees next Thursday's **TSM** earnings as an important guide on orders. He writes that **Palantir** set a new record and that those who shorted following Michael Burry lost again; he argues the April 2025 drop was harder than 2026 so far and questions why **PayPal** and **Nike** remain in the index. He says he holds a small position in **EOSE** and is holding patiently.

holdings.name: SoFi Technologies
holdings.opinion: About a fifth of the portfolio sits in a single stock; as a rate-sensitive growth/financial name, the jump in bond yields is the main risk and concentration the second.
ai_points: Against: at roughly 20% weight there is single-stock concentration.
Against: according to Defiant Gatekeeper the 10-year yield is at its highest since 2006, a pressure for rate-sensitive stocks.
For: there is no SoFi-specific negative news in today's sources.

holdings.name: Broadcom

mentions.quote: $161 billion will go to Broadcom for custom chips.

holdings.why: According to Bora Özkent, $161 billion of Anthropic's $518 billion infrastructure spend goes to Broadcom's custom chips, but there is no new buy/sell trigger.
holdings.opinion: Anthropic's commitments give Broadcom visibility, but financing that demand depends on Anthropic's IPO and its ability to raise cash; this week's OpenAI revenue report showed how sensitive semiconductor stocks are.
ai_points: For: according to Bora Özkent, $161 billion of Anthropic's custom-chip spending goes to Broadcom.
Against: Özkent says about 80% of this spending is binding and its financing is uncertain.
Against: according to cevikfinance, semiconductors (SMH) ended the week down 4.3%.

holdings.name: BWX Technologies

Against: according to Ahmet Sunelcan, the US defense budget runs on a stopgap budget valid until December 11.
Against: there is no BWX-specific news in today's sources.
